findings.finding: 5 of the new tests use source-inspection (inspect.getsource) rather than behavioral testing. While they serve as regression guards against specific code-structure mistakes, they are fragile: a refactor renaming 'round_counter' or restructuring indentation would cause false failures even when behavior is correct. The plan explicitly asked to 'drive _run_cluster_islands (or just _should_migrate_this_round directly) with n_clusters=3, interval=2' — only the parametrized test on _should_migrate_this_round does this behaviorally. The loop-level test (test_migration_cadence_uses_rounds_not_clusters) is source-inspection only.

Commit message on 0c8d014 mentions only 'define n_clusters' but the commit includes all three fixes (seed collision, migration cadence, n_clusters). Future readers of git blame may be confused about when the seed/migration changes were introduced.

positive_observations: Item 6 (seed collision): _derive_island_seed called with direction prefix at both call sites — f"{direction}_{cid}" (line 424) and f"{direction}_orphan_{sym}" (line 326). direction is a string parameter in scope at both sites. Signature unchanged. Seed uniqueness tests use real _derive_island_seed values, not mock assertions.

Item 7 (migration cadence): _should_migrate_this_round is a clean pure function with correct docstring. Handles edge cases (interval <= 0 → False, round_index=0 % interval=0 → True). round_counter increments once per outer while loop (line 461), NOT inside the for-cid loop. All epoch_counter references purged from production code.

n_clusters fix: n_clusters = len(cluster_ids) placed correctly at line 401, immediately after cluster_ids is sorted. AST verified: 1 assignment, 2 references (the second is in 'and n_clusters > 1' at the migration guard). Regression tests for this exist.

Parametrized test (test_should_migrate_this_round_parametrized) covers 14 cases including edge cases: interval=0 (never fires), interval=-1 (never fires), interval=1 (always fires), interval=2, interval=3 with various round_index values. This is the strongest test in the set.

Edge cases covered: base_seed=None returns None (test_derive_island_seed_none_input_returns_none), signature unchanged verified (test_derive_island_seed_signature_unchanged), interval <= 0 handled in helper.
No dead code: zero epoch_counter references in production code (grep confirmed). No unused imports introduced.
All 53 tests pass (39 test_phase2_island_scheduler + 4 test_island_scheduler_migration + 10 test_migration_safety). 130/131 pass in test_phase2_rule_pool (1 pre-existing, unrelated failure).

Backward compatibility: _derive_island_seed signature unchanged. Seed values will differ (intentional bug fix), but no tests depend on exact historical seed values — test_derive_island_seed_distinct_for_distinct_ids in test_phase2_rule_pool.py checks uniqueness, not exact values.
notes: The implementation is correct across all three fixes. The seed collision fix and migration cadence fix address real, reproducible bugs. The n_clusters NameError introduced by Task 1 is properly resolved. The test strategy could be stronger — 5 source-inspection tests are fragile and the plan's explicit request for a behavioral loop-drive test was only partially satisfied (the parametrized test on _should_migrate_this_round, while excellent, is the helper function in isolation, not the full loop). However, the combination of isolation tests on the helper + source-inspection regression guards + all existing integration-level tests passing provides adequate coverage for the risk level of these changes. No blocking issues.
